paragraphs.title: Thanksgiving and Joy in God’s Deliverance

easy.explanation: Psalm 9:1 says, “I will praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart.”
easy.q: With what does the psalmist praise the LORD?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will be glad and rejoice in thee.”
easy.q: In whom does the psalmist rejoice?

answers: A song of victory over Israel
easy.explanation: He declares, “I will sing praise to thy name, O thou most High.”
easy.q: What will the psalmist sing to God’s name?

medium.explanation: Verse 3 says, “they shall fall and perish at thy presence.”
medium.q: What happens to the enemies when they turn back?

medium.explanation: He says, “I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist say he will show forth?

answers: Because God maintains his right and judges righteously
Because God gives him earthly riches
Because his enemies ask for advice
medium.explanation: God has maintained the psalmist’s cause and sits on the throne judging right.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist praise God according to these verses?

answers: God’s righteous judgment gives the psalmist reason to praise Him
challenge.explanation: The psalmist praises God while describing His judgment and deliverance from enemies.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between God’s judgment and the psalmist’s praise?

challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes wholehearted, complete praise.
challenge.q: What does “with my whole heart” emphasize?

answers: As one seated on the throne judging right
As the ruler of one city only
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “thou satest in the throne judging right.”
challenge.q: How is God presented in verse 4?

paragraphs.title: The Enemy’s Defeat and God’s Reign of Justice

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “thou hast destroyed the wicked.”
easy.q: What has the LORD done to the wicked?

answers: They were destroyed and their memorial perished
easy.explanation: The enemy’s cities were destroyed, and their memorial was forgotten.
Verse 7 says, “the LORD shall endure for ever.”
easy.q: How long shall the LORD endure?

answers: The enemies disappear, but the LORD endures for ever
The enemies endure, but the LORD disappears
Both the enemies and the LORD are temporary
medium.explanation: The enemies’ memorial perishes, while the LORD endures forever.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the enemies and the LORD?

medium.explanation: God has prepared His throne for judgment.
medium.q: What does God’s throne represent in these verses?

medium.explanation: He will judge the world “in righteousness” and the people “in uprightness.”
medium.q: How will the LORD judge the world?

answers: The temporary nature of human power compared with God’s permanence
That the enemies are equal to God
challenge.explanation: The enemies vanish, while the LORD remains enthroned forever.
challenge.q: What does the destruction of the enemy’s memorial emphasize?

challenge.explanation: The words “righteousness” and “uprightness” describe God’s just judgment.
challenge.q: What qualities of God’s judgment are highlighted?

answers: It shows that His rule and judgment are permanent
It shows that He has abandoned the nations
challenge.explanation: The enduring throne portrays God’s lasting authority over judgment.
challenge.q: Why is the LORD’s enduring throne significant?

paragraphs.title: God as a Refuge for the Afflicted and a Call to Proclaim His Salvation

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed.”
easy.q: What is the LORD for the oppressed?

answers: Sing praises and declare God’s doings
easy.explanation: They are told to sing praises and declare among the people His doings.
easy.q: What are the people called to do in Zion?

answers: Have mercy and consider his trouble
easy.explanation: He prays, “Have mercy upon me, O LORD; consider my trouble.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

answers: So that he may show forth God’s praise
So that he may build a city
So that he may forget God
medium.explanation: He asks for deliverance so he can proclaim God’s praise.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask to be lifted from the gates of death?

answers: A place of safety and protection
medium.explanation: A refuge is a place of shelter and protection in trouble.
medium.q: What does “refuge” mean in these verses?

medium.explanation: Verse 10 says, “they that know thy name will put their trust in thee.”
medium.q: What do those who know God’s name do?

answers: The psalmist seeks deliverance so he can proclaim God’s praise
The psalmist wants mercy so he can stop worshipping
The verses connect mercy with silence
challenge.explanation: He asks to be lifted from death’s gates so he may show forth God’s praise.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between God’s mercy and the psalmist’s praise?

answers: God’s salvation should be publicly proclaimed
God’s works should remain a private secret
Only kings may speak of God
challenge.explanation: The command to declare His doings calls for open testimony.
challenge.q: What does declaring God’s works among the people imply?

answers: He is their refuge and does not forsake those who seek Him
He abandons them in times of trouble
challenge.explanation: The LORD is a refuge and does not forsake those who seek Him.
challenge.q: How do these verses portray God’s relationship with the afflicted?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked Are Caught by Their Own Deeds

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “The heathen are sunk down in the pit that they made.”
easy.q: Where are the heathen sunk down?

easy.explanation: The wicked are “snared in the work of his own hands.”
easy.q: What happens to the wicked in the work of their own hands?

answers: Into the gates of the city
easy.explanation: Verse 17 says, “The wicked shall be turned into hell.”
easy.q: Where shall the wicked be turned?

medium.explanation: The net was hidden by them, yet their own foot was taken in it.
medium.q: Why are the heathen caught in the net?

answers: The LORD is known by the judgment He executes
The wicked are stronger than God
medium.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD is known by the judgment which he executeth.”
medium.q: What is revealed by the wicked being caught?

medium.explanation: Verse 17 refers to “all the nations that forget God.”
medium.q: Who is said to forget God?

answers: People may suffer the consequences of their own wicked deeds
challenge.explanation: The trap prepared by the wicked becomes the means of their own capture.
challenge.q: What moral principle is illustrated by the pit and net?

answers: The judgment described in verse 15 is shown in the wicked being caught
challenge.explanation: The wicked’s capture demonstrates the LORD’s judgment.
challenge.q: How does verse 16 relate to verse 15?

answers: The needy will not always be forgotten, while the wicked face judgment
The needy are identified as those who forget God
challenge.explanation: The following verse promises that the needy will not always be forgotten, unlike the nations that forget God.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the needy and those who forget God?

paragraphs.title: Hope for the Poor and a Prayer for God’s Revelation

easy.explanation: Verse 18 says, “the needy shall not alway be forgotten.”
easy.q: Who shall not always be forgotten?
What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: The psalmist asks that the nations know themselves “to be but men.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist want the nations to know?

answers: So that man will not prevail and the nations will be judged
So that the wicked will become stronger
So that judgment will be hidden
medium.explanation: He asks God to prevent man from prevailing and to judge the nations.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD to arise?

answers: Human beings should not triumph arrogantly over God’s justice
The poor should rule every nation
medium.explanation: The prayer asks God to restrain human arrogance and power.
medium.q: What does “let not man prevail” mean in context?

answers: Because the poor will not be forgotten, the psalmist asks God to act in judgment
The hope of the poor requires forgetting God
medium.explanation: The promise concerning the needy leads into a prayer for God’s intervention.
medium.q: How are the hope of the poor and the prayer connected?

challenge.explanation: The phrase “but men” stresses human limitation.
challenge.q: What should the nations understand about themselves?

answers: Human arrogance versus recognition of God’s authority
challenge.explanation: The prayer asks God to restrain human pride and reveal humanity’s proper place.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in these verses?

answers: With a request that they recognize they are only human
With a declaration that they are stronger than God
With a command to build cities
challenge.explanation: The closing request is that the nations know themselves to be but men.
challenge.q: How does the psalm end in relation to humanity and the nations?
